refValue.description: absent = not yet researched; null = confirmed none; string or list = the reference(s)

url.description: a locator: a bare URL, never an archive wrapper (web.archive.org/web/<ts>/...) — ingest unwraps those into url + as_of; enforced by validate.py

date.description: contest date at the precision known: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD

location.description: free-text place(s) as imported (sheet / CMS site labels joined by '; '); kept until `sites` covers everything, then dropped

venue.description: unused (reserved); the venue is the institution node in `sites`

sites.description: where the contest was held, one entry per site: a node of locations.yaml (institution, city, region or country) plus the site's own label when it is not simply the institution. `location` (free text) stays alongside until sites cover every contest; `venue` is unused. DEFINITIONS.md, Locations

sources.description: the contest's catalogued addresses, each with its roles. Absence of a role here and in `none` = not yet researched

none.description: roles confirmed to have no source (looked, there is none) — replaces the old `field: null`

provenance.description: where the facts on this entry came from (free text, one line each)

asOf.description: Wayback-style timestamp, 4-14 digits at the precision known (2011, 20110102, 20110102183612): the content meant is what the locator served at this time (live address dead/repurposed). Derivable wayback link: web.archive.org/web/<as_of>/<url>

problemsBlock.description: link to the problem set this contest used (problemsets/<set-id>.yaml holds the problems, holdings and letter maps; DEFINITIONS.md, Problems)

role.description: what a source holds. Result roles rank scoreboard > frozen_scoreboard > standings > rankings > icpc_standings by information content; web = the contest website; teams = team list; problemset = the published set; problem = one problem's statement; judge_page = an online judge's page holding the contest's problems (requires `judge`)

source.description: a catalogued address (DEFINITIONS.md, Resources): one entry per URL, however many roles it serves

also_at.description: other addresses serving the same content (organiser archive copies, mirrors), bare or {url, as_of}; the capture queue fetches them, snapshots obtained there are snapshots of this source via that mirror

judge.description: for judge_page: the judge id (kattis, livearchive, baekjoon, codeforces, ...)

archived.description: archive references of captures of this address: <contest-id>/<kind>/<fetch-date>/...; a list because one address is often captured under several roles

url_state.description: health of the address at url_checked

locationId.description: id of a node in locations.yaml (schema/locations.schema.json); resolution checked by validate.py

site.description: one site of a contest. {type: administrative} alone is the CMS's bookkeeping site (no place); {type: online} is a remote site, with a location when the organiser is known; an entry with `name` but no `location` is a site the tool could not place (listed in data/locations-review-*.md)

location.description: the most specific node known: institution when known, else city, region or country

name.description: the site's label as the CMS gives it, kept when it is not just the institution's or city's name (division labels, 'Perth Schools', team groups)

date.description: the site's own date when it differs from the contest date (multi-day or staggered sites)

type.description: administrative: the CMS's non-physical bookkeeping site (staff, hidden teams, 'Administrative Site Location'); online: teams competed remotely

tier.description: world-finals; championship (continental layer skipped when deriving hierarchy depth); regional (advances to a WF or a championship); subregional (advances to a regional: qualifiers, national and site rounds, regional-level views of a division)

region.description: ICPC super-region the series belongs to (championships: the one they are the championship of; absent for the World Finals)

naming.description: which half of the season the year in contest ids names: season-start (fall regionals: nwerc-2018 is in season 2019) or season-end (World Finals, championships). A delayed or early edition keeps the pattern.
